target.title: fix(telegram): distinguish and render streamed reasoning/commentary progress lanes
target.body: ## What Problem This Solves Fixes an issue where Telegram users watching a streamed reply could not tell the model's **reasoning** apart from its **commentary** in the live progress box, and saw the model's raw Markdown (`**`, backticks) as literal characters. On current `main`, the two streamed progress lanes render identically — this is the exact HTML the bot sends to Telegram for one turn: ``` Barnacling Running `date`, then reading AGENTS.md ← reasoning **Step 1: Running `date`.** ← commentary ``` Both lanes are italic with no distinguishing marker, so they're indistinguishable, and the model's Markdown leaks raw. This is most visible with deepseek, which narrates almost entirely through its reasoning lane. Separately, on fast turns the streaming "gerund" progress box was deleted the instant the turn ended, so it flashed and vanished before it could be read (and the delete could race a just-persisted message, intermittently dropping the first verbose commentary line). ## Why This Change Was Made The shared progress-draft compositor already supports per-channel lane markers, but the Telegram channel wasn't passing them, and its progress renderer hand-rolled HTML (only `_italic_`, everything else HTML-escaped) instead of using the same Markdown→Telegram-HTML converter the final answer uses. Two focused fixes: 1. **Lane rendering** — pass the `🧠`/`💬` lane prefixes and `commentaryItalics: false` to the compositor (mirroring the Discord channel), and route the reasoning/commentary lane bodies through the shared `markdownToTelegramRichHtml`. Reasoning renders `🧠` + italic; commentary renders `💬` + plain, with `**bold**`, inline code, and links rendered rather than leaked. Generic item payloads keep their monospace styling; HTML parse errors still degrade to plain text via the existing draft-stream fallback. 2. **Preview lifetime** — keep the streaming preview on screen for at least 4s from when it first appeared, deleting it detached (scheduled via `setTimeout`, never awaited) so turn teardown is never stalled. Non-goals: this does not touch the final answer rendering or the durable (`/verbose on`) lanes — only the streamed progress window. ## User Impact Telegram users watching a streamed reply now see reasoning (🧠, italic) clearly distinct from commentary (💬, plain), with the model's Markdown rendered as bold/code/links instead of raw `**`/backticks, and the progress box stays readable for at least 4 seconds instead of flashing away on fast turns. Biggest improvement for deepseek. After this change, the same turn renders: ``` Barnacling 🧠 Running date, then reading AGENTS.md 💬 Step 1: Running date. ``` ## Evidence **Before/after payload** — exact HTML the bot sends to Telegram for the same input, captured through the real dispatch path (see the two blocks above): reasoning gains the `🧠` marker, commentary gains `💬` and is no longer italic (so the lanes are distinct), and `**`/backticks render instead of leaking. **Live Telegram** (dev bot, anthropic sonnet, reasoning-stream) — reasoning lane, before vs after: | Before (`main`) | After (this PR) | | --- | --- | | ![before](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Marvinthebored/openclaw/proof-assets-telegram-progress-lanes/telegram-streamed-progress-lanes/reasoning-lane-before.png) | ![after](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Marvinthebored/openclaw/proof-assets-telegram-progress-lanes/telegram-streamed-progress-lanes/reasoning-lane-after.png) | Before shows plain reasoning with no marker; after shows the `🧠` marker and italic reasoning. **Tests** — `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs extensions/telegram/src/bot-message-dispatch.test.ts extensions/telegram/src/draft-stream.test.ts` → 2 files, **195 passed**. Includes a new `renders model markdown in streamed reasoning and commentary lanes` test (asserts the exact after-HTML above) and a new `keeps the streaming preview on screen for the dwell window before deleting` test.
